clue.text: God of love after a ballot

indicators.note: after places the word before it behind the phrase that follows, so the love piece goes last

blocks.note: taken as written
a poll is a ballot or vote
love is nil in tennis, and nil looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A deity of romance turns up once the votes are cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'God of love' reads as Cupid or Eros, but only 'God' is the definition; 'of love' is the O that comes after A POLL.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo is the Greek and Roman god of music, light and prophecy.

clue.text: Piece of music composed to greet all

indicators.note: to compose is to put together or arrange, so the letters that follow are set in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tune written as a welcome to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegretto is a movement or passage played fairly briskly, so it names a piece of music.

clue.text: Defeat old-fashioned party

blocks.note: something out of date is said to be out
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Beating an unfashionable political party at the polls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests a political party, but here it is a celebration, a do.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to surpass or beat them, so it is a verb synonym for defeat.

clue.text: Composer shown round very European port

indicators.note: being shown round means wrapping around something else, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: Franz Lehár composed The Merry Widow
V is the standard abbreviation for very
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A musician is given a tour of a thoroughly continental harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: Franz Lehár is a favourite crossword composer; the container takes the very-letter, and the European-letter tails on outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Havre is a major French seaport on the English Channel.

clue.text: Ethnic, first in box in court case

indicators.note: the first in a word means only its opening letter is kept
one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a trial is a case heard in court
the opening letter of box

explanation.surface: An ethnic dispute is the main item boxed up in a court action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' sounds like the witness box in a court case, but only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal describes things belonging to a tribe or people, a near synonym of ethnic.

clue.text: Note girl drinking drop of sparkling wine

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, so only one letter, the first, is taken
someone drinking takes something inside, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a girl's name
the first letter of sparkling

explanation.surface: A young woman sips a little fizz from her glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sparkling wine' reads as champagne, but the answer is a still Greek wine; 'sparkling' only lends its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Beans are, I suspect, served up in a sauce

indicators.note: something suspect is dubious and not to be taken as it stands, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner suspects the beans have arrived drowned in sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Béarnaise is a classic French sauce of butter, egg yolk, vinegar and tarragon.

clue.text: Enjoy the same thing

blocks.note: first meaning: to be fond of
second meaning: a counterpart or equal

explanation.surface: Two people find pleasure in an identical pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for being fond of and a noun for a similar thing, as in 'we shall not see its like again'.

clue.text: Some tinsel, at Christmas, in bar

indicators.note: some of a phrase is only part of it, so the answer is a run of letters within the words

blocks.note: spans the end of tinsel, all of at and the start of Christmas

explanation.surface: Decorations put up in a pub over the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub to go with the tinsel, but here it is a fastening on a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A latch is a simple bar that fastens a door or gate.

clue.text: Divert sports team approaching course

blocks.note: a side is a team
a track is a course for racing

explanation.surface: A team bus is rerouted as it nears the racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidetrack someone is to divert their attention away from the main issue.

clue.text: Second-rate vessel in need of flag

blocks.note: a sub, short for submarine, is a vessel
a standard is a flag or banner

explanation.surface: A shabby ship lacks a proper ensign to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Substandard means below the expected level, just as second-rate does.

clue.text: Sketch popular stable lad in reception area

blocks.note: to draw is to sketch
what is in is fashionable and popular
a groom looks after horses in a stable

explanation.surface: An artist draws a well-liked stable hand in a hotel lobby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sketch' looks like it gives DRAWING whole, leaving nothing for 'popular'; it is only DRAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawing room is a room for receiving and entertaining guests, so it is a reception area.

clue.text: Suitable, "Feelings", a pop single

blocks.note: good can mean fit or suitable
vibrations, or vibes, are feelings or atmosphere

explanation.surface: A record review says a song titled Feelings fits the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'Feelings' look like the song's title, but it is only a synonym in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Good Vibrations was a famous 1966 hit single by the Beach Boys.

clue.text: Nobleman holding a dart and a toy weapon

indicators.note: something holding another thing has it inside, so one piece encloses the next

blocks.note: a peer is a member of the nobility
taken as written
to dart is to shoot, move swiftly

explanation.surface: A lord clutches a dart and a child's plaything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dart' looks like a missile to go with the weapon, but it is the verb, to shoot or dash. PE(A SHOOT)ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A peashooter is a small tube for blowing dried peas, a children's toy weapon.

clue.text: Intensely serious, boy describing adult

indicators.note: to describe is also to draw around, as with a circle, so one piece encircles another

blocks.note: a boy's name
A is the film certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A solemn lad gives an account of a grown-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' is used in its geometric sense, to draw a line around something.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means sincere and deeply serious in intent, the same as intensely serious.

clue.text: Ashore, son plays in a North Wales resort

indicators.note: playing with things means moving them about, so the letters get a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: On land, a young man enjoys himself at a Welsh seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhos-on-Sea is a seaside town near Colwyn Bay on the North Wales coast.

clue.text: Fancy goods originally imported by one US state

indicators.note: originally points to the origin of a word, its first letter
something imported is brought inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Maine is a north-eastern US state
the first letter of goods

explanation.surface: A single American state brings in luxury merchandise from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy goods' reads as one phrase, but 'Fancy' alone is the definition, used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something can mean to suppose or picture it in the mind, which is to imagine it.

clue.text: Remarkably smooth northern newspaper proprietor

indicators.note: remarkably suggests something done in an unusual way, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A press baron from the north is unusually suave.
explanation.definitionFit: Roy Thomson, Lord Thomson of Fleet, owned The Times and The Sunday Times.

clue.text: Defiant remark made by chronic drunkard in this place

blocks.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
here means in this place

explanation.surface: A boozer in a bar makes a defiant comment.
explanation.definitionFit: "So there!" is a childish retort said to show defiance after making one's point.

clue.text: Understands article in rag's racy

indicators.note: racy means lively and risqué, suggesting letters that will not sit still in their order
one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, with the apostrophe dropped
the definite article

explanation.surface: A reader grasps that an item in the tabloid is rather saucy.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag is slang for a low-quality newspaper; 'article' looks like a newspaper item but is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather can mean to infer or understand, as in 'I gather you've been away'.

clue.text: Tart, upper part containing bread

indicators.note: something containing another holds it inside, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: the top is the upper part of anything
a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: A pastry with a top crust filled with bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' and 'bread' suggest baking, but the tart is a person here. T(ROLL)OP.
explanation.definitionFit: Trollop is a dated insult for a promiscuous woman, the same slang sense as tart.

clue.text: Both row rowboat unsuitably loaded

indicators.note: unsuitably means in the wrong way, so the letters are put out of their proper order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Two people both row a boat that is badly overladen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaded' sits with the boat as cargo, but it is slang for rich. A bob was an old British shilling.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone worth a bob or two is well off, and loaded is slang for very wealthy.

clue.text: Faint-hearted gloomy Italian turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning something up makes it read from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: dim means dark or gloomy
It is the abbreviation for Italian

explanation.surface: A shy, melancholy Italian appears at the door.
explanation.walkthrough: DIM + IT read backwards gives TIMID, a neat reversal in a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Timid means lacking courage, which is what faint-hearted describes.

clue.text: Record throw

blocks.note: first meaning: to register
second meaning: to fling or hurl

explanation.surface: A world-record throw at an athletics meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one noun phrase, but each word is a separate verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast means to fling, and also to register, as in casting a vote.

clue.text: Mater's rewritten: Mother, with a capital

indicators.note: something rewritten is set down afresh, so its letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
a dam is the mother of an animal

explanation.surface: Mum's letter is rewritten by Mother with a capital letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mater' is old public-school slang for mother, which makes 'Mother' look like its partner; here it is DAM, used of livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Amsterdam is the capital city of the Netherlands.

clue.text: Confine one male brought in drunk

indicators.note: something brought in is taken inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: lit is slang for drunk
I is the Roman numeral one
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A drunken man is locked up after being hauled in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought in' suggests an arrest, but it only signals one piece going inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: To limit is to restrict or keep within bounds, which is to confine.

clue.text: Make a journey with French composer after end of concert

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of concert
Maurice Ravel, French composer of Boléro

explanation.surface: Travelling with a French composer once the concert is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To travel is to go from one place to another, which is making a journey.

clue.text: Here's the spinner - there'll be flipping ducks again!

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it round, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to duck is to dip or plunge under

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator groans that the spin bowler will bring more batting failures.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a spinner is a slow bowler and a duck is a score of nought; 'flipping' reads as a mild British curse.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider spins silk to make its web, so it is the spinner.
